title: R.E.P.O. Items and Tools: Three Staff Effects Explained
description: A concise reference to the Zero Gravity, Roll, and Void Staff effects documented in the existing R.E.P.O. patch notes.
lead: The official v0.4.4 notes describe three specific staffs and give all staffs six battery pips. Use the current item description for any effect or cost not listed here.
steps: Zero Gravity Staff is more controllable on non-enemy objects and can move the user when self-cast. Its documented use here is repositioning an object or the player, not an invented damage value.
Roll Staff makes rolling objects target enemies. Self-use gives the player camera-steered rolling; check the space ahead before choosing that movement.
Void Staff pulls heavy objects more strongly and creates outward surges near its center. Keep important valuables away from an uncontrolled pull lane.
All staffs have six battery pips in v0.4.4. Read the current item and shop display for availability, price, and any later changes.
mistakes: Treating a staff's object interaction as a universal enemy counter, or copying a pre-v0.4.4 battery description.
versionNote: These are documented v0.4.4 effects, not a complete item database or a current shop inventory.

title: Apex Predator (Duck): create space before you counter
description: The Duck dossier: recognize the threat, protect the carrier, and avoid a bad chase.
lead: The yellow duck is harmless until picked up or damaged; then it becomes a fast chaser for a short window. The Enemy Index already records the trigger and counter, so this page stays brief.
steps: Do not pick up or damage the duck when the route does not require it.
If it has transformed, leave the item recoverable and use the Enemy Index dossier for the documented environment or Duck Bucket counter with a clear exit.
mistakes: Picking up the duck casually or committing to a counter without an exit.
versionNote: Monster behavior and counter reliability are version-sensitive. Use this as conservative route advice rather than an exact timing reference.

title: Trudge: route around the pull
description: Keep large valuables and the return path out of the danger zone.
lead: Trudge can pull players and large valuables into a close-range strike. Official v0.4.4 notes changed its suction to Void Staff-style behavior, making larger valuables easier to pull. Park the load outside that lane before crossing.
steps: Recognize the grinding mace audio and ground vibration described in the Enemy Index dossier.
Park large valuables outside the pull lane. The v0.4.4 change means older footage of heavy-object behavior may not describe the current pull.
Wait for an open crossing instead of fighting in a choke point; consult the dossier for the short counter.
mistakes: Leaving a large valuable in the pull lane or using old heavy-object footage as a timing chart.
versionNote: Official v0.4.4 notes changed Trudge’s suck behavior, so older footage is useful for ideas but not for exact timing.

title: Tick: do not carry blindly
description: A small threat becomes dangerous when the carrier loses control of the item.
lead: A Tick can latch onto a player handling an object and drain health. The Enemy Index dossier already has the recognition cue and counter; keep the carry response short here.
steps: Put the valuable down outside the contact area instead of forcing a carry through the latch.
Create space and use the Tick dossier in the Enemy Index before resuming the item route.
mistakes: Keeping the valuable in hand while the Tick is attaching.
versionNote: Community guides disagree on some attack conditions and damage details. Use the conservative handling rule here and treat exact triggers as version-sensitive.

title: Duo strategy: split focus, not the run
description: A two-player plan for scouting, hauling, callouts, and extraction.
lead: With two players, one handles the valuable and C.A.R.T. while the other checks the next doorway and return route. Swap at a safe handoff when the carrier needs to scout.
steps: Choose which player carries and which checks the next room and truck route before moving the first valuable.
Keep the C.A.R.T. near the current work area. If the carrier needs to inspect an unknown doorway, set the item down and swap roles at that handoff.
At extraction, one player adjusts the load inside the boundary while the other watches the return path and remaining objective.
mistakes: Both players entering an unscouted room with valuables and leaving nobody to check the return lane.
versionNote: Role recommendations are strategy guidance, not game rules; map layout, monster density, and player skill change the best split.

title: How Many Players Can Play R.E.P.O.? Max Player Count and Team Roles
description: Learn R.E.P.O.'s up to 6-player online co-op limit and practical team roles for groups of two to six.
lead: R.E.P.O. supports up to six players in online co-op. The official Steam page describes the game as playable with up to five friends, meaning you plus five other players. Smaller groups can still play; you do not need a six-player lobby.
steps: How Many Players Can Play R.E.P.O.? R.E.P.O. supports up to 6 players total in online multiplayer. The official Steam description says you can venture into the game with up to five friends: 1 player + 5 friends = 6 players total. You do not need six people to start playing.

Can You Play R.E.P.O. With 2 Players? Yes. A two-player group can split basic responsibilities between scouting, carrying, watching the route, and reacting to enemies. With fewer players, each player has to cover more jobs.

Can You Play R.E.P.O. With 3 or 4 Players? Yes. This is where defined roles become more useful. For three players, use one scout, one hauler, and one flexible support player. With four players, an additional player can focus more heavily on extraction, enemy distraction, or protecting the return route.

What About 5 or 6 Players? Larger groups give you more people for carrying and enemy control, but more players do not automatically make a run organized. Keep distinct responsibilities: a scout, one or more carriers, route awareness, and recovery or defensive support.

Is R.E.P.O. 6-Player Co-op? Yes. Six players is the current official maximum described on the Steam store page. That does not mean six players are required. Use the team size you actually have and adjust roles around the current map, valuables, enemies, and return route.
mistakes: Everyone looting, nobody owning the return route, and letting proximity voice break the team into isolated pairs.
versionNote: The role matrix comes from community strategy guides and should be adjusted for the current map, player skill, and patch.

title: Headman Manor: route, risks, and extraction plan
description: A focused map guide for a vertical, cluttered, high-collision layout.
lead: Headman Manor rewards a cautious staging plan. Clear a route through the vertical rooms, use the cart to protect fragile value, and leave noisy or awkward valuables until the return path is known.
steps: Find the main stair and the safest cart staging point before chasing high-value rooms.
Clear doorways and corners for large objects before attempting a heavy carry.
Treat noisy valuables as an alert decision: call the room, prepare the retreat, then pick up.
Use vertical shortcuts only when the landing and recovery route are visible.
Finish the safest extraction points first and reserve the return route for the crew, not extra loot.
mistakes: Trying to move a piano or clock through a blind corner, carrying without a cart staging point, and assuming a high room is worth the fall risk.
versionNote: Map-specific routes need current screenshots or footage. This page uses community map descriptions and is a route framework, not a fixed seed.

title: Health, Stamina, and Range: when each matters
description: Choose the stat that changes your route instead of buying a generic comfort pick.
lead: Health can absorb a repeated hit; Stamina supports movement and actions on the same route; Range matters when a pickup or interaction is unsafe at the current distance. The repo does not establish numerical efficiency for any of them.
steps: Choose Health if damage repeatedly ends an otherwise workable route; check whether the same hit is survived on the next comparable run.
Choose Stamina if movement or carrying repeatedly runs out before the crew can reach safety; keep an escape reserve on the same route.
Choose Range when extra interaction distance changes a specific pickup or control position. If it does not change that angle, save for a different offer.
mistakes: Buying Range without a specific safer interaction angle or comparing old prices as current shop facts.
versionNote: Effect summaries are stable strategy guidance; exact increments and price ranges must be retested on the current build.

title: R.E.P.O. v0.4.4 patch notes: what changed for players
description: The v0.4.4 update improves melee handling at higher Strength, adds one second of protection after revival, updates all staffs, and makes Trudge more disruptive around large valuables.
lead: The biggest v0.4.4 changes affect recovery and object control. Revived players get a brief safety window, melee weapons respond more firmly at higher Strength, all staffs use six battery pips, and Trudge now pulls large valuables with Void Staff-style suction.
steps: Melee weapons now scale their handling correctly with Strength. Higher Strength should make them feel firmer, but it does not replace spacing or a safe attack angle.
A revived player receives one second of invincibility. Use that moment to move out of immediate danger; do not treat it as a long damage window.
All staffs now have six battery pips. Zero Gravity Staff is more controllable on non-enemy objects and can move the user when self-cast.
Roll Staff makes rolling objects target enemies, while self-use gives the player camera-steered rolling. Void Staff pulls heavy objects more strongly and creates outward surges near its center.
Trudge now uses Void Staff-style suction, pulling larger valuables more easily and creating more chaos near the center. Park important loot farther from its pull lane.
Vehicle interaction areas around buttons were reduced to limit accidental activation; take care when grabbing a vehicle near its button.
mistakes: Assuming the revive protection lasts long enough to stand still, leaving heavy valuables near Trudge, using old staff battery or behavior advice after updating, and grabbing a vehicle carelessly beside its button.
versionNote: Official v0.4.4 notes were published May 25, 2026. Check the version shown by the game before applying these changes to a later build.

title: R.E.P.O. upgrade planner
description: Choose a crew role and the problem that ended your last run to get one upgrade priority, a fallback, and a practical check for the next attempt.
lead: Use the interactive planner below. It gives decision support rather than a fixed tier list, and it never assumes a shop item is available.
steps: Select the crew size, the role receiving the purchase, and the failure that ended the run.
Read the primary priority and compare it with the upgrades or tools actually available at the Service Station.
Use the fallback when the first category is unavailable or the role does not need it.
Follow the next-run check to see whether the purchase solved the named problem.
Change one variable at a time; choose a different failure only when the previous bottleneck is no longer ending runs.
mistakes: Choosing a universal tier-list favorite instead of the current bottleneck, buying a team tool without assigning a user, and changing several unrelated variables at once.
versionNote: The planner avoids fixed prices, caps, and guaranteed shop availability because those details can change by version and run.

title: R.E.P.O. FAQ: quota, extraction, upgrades, monsters, and co-op
description: Direct answers to common early-run questions, with links to the full guides for each system.
lead: Quota tells you how much value the current objective needs; extraction and leaving are separate steps. Buy around the failure ending your runs, and treat monsters as route problems before treating them as fights.
steps: Do I need to clear the whole map? No. Satisfy the displayed objective and leave when the extra loot is not worth the route risk.
Why can’t we leave immediately after reaching quota? Wait for the automatic extraction sequence to finish, then regroup at the truck and follow the current departure prompt.
What should I buy first? Choose the upgrade or tool that addresses the repeated failure: carrying, stamina, damage, reach, control, or fragile value.
Should we fight every monster? No. Identify its trigger, protect the loot lane, and fight only when it blocks the route and the crew has a safe setup.
How should co-op roles work? Assign navigation, carrying, and lookout duties, but let players switch when the room or current load changes.

How Much Is R.E.P.O.? As of September 2026, R.E.P.O.'s standard U.S. Steam price is $9.99. Steam sales can temporarily reduce that price, and regional pricing can differ by country. Because R.E.P.O. is still in Early Access, this price is not guaranteed to stay unchanged forever. The developer has said the price may increase when the game reaches version 1.0. RUNBACK treats $9.99 as the current U.S. base price rather than a permanent lifetime price.

Is R.E.P.O. Free? No. R.E.P.O. is currently a paid Steam game, not a free-to-play game. Temporary discounts do not make the game permanently free. If you see a different price, check the current Steam listing because discounts and regional pricing can change.
mistakes: Treating quota as a full-clear order, assuming one purchase order fits every crew, and chasing a monster after the route is already safe.
versionNote: Prompts, shops, enemy behavior, and multiplayer interactions can change. The linked focused guides carry the version-specific caveats.

title: What is R.E.P.O.? Story, setting, and confirmed details
description: R.E.P.O. is an online co-op horror game where physics-based valuables must be retrieved and extracted while monsters threaten the crew and its cargo.
lead: The game casts players as Semibots sent to retrieve valuable objects from abandoned environments. The immediate story is communicated through the Taxman, objectives, locations, and environmental details; explanations beyond what the game or developer confirms should be treated as interpretation.
steps: The official premise is retrieval: locate valuable, fully physics-based objects and extract enough value to satisfy your creator.
The Semibots work as a crew, with the gameplay supporting up to six online players.
The Taxman frames quota and progression, but the game leaves much of the wider world and the fate of its human spaces implicit.
Rooms, props, valuables, shop interactions, and enemy designs provide environmental clues without establishing every fan theory as canon.
When a theory explains the creator, locations, or monsters, separate what appears on screen from what the community infers.
mistakes: Presenting a fan theory as confirmed lore, treating a joke or item description as a complete timeline, and confusing gameplay terminology with an official story explanation.
versionNote: This page stays with the official premise and visible environmental storytelling. Future developer statements or major updates may add confirmed context.

title: Is R.E.P.O. on PS5 or Xbox? Console Release & Crossplay Status
description: Is R.E.P.O. on PS5 or Xbox? Check the current console release status, crossplay support, PC availability, and what semiwork has said about future console versions.
lead: R.E.P.O. is currently available on Windows PC through Steam. Developer semiwork says a console release is part of the current plan, but the team does not expect to fully work on it until development is closer to the 1.0 release. There is currently no confirmed PS5 or Xbox release date, and PC-to-console crossplay is not available because no console version has been released yet.
steps: Is R.E.P.O. on PS5? No. As of September 2026, R.E.P.O. does not have a released PS5 version. semiwork has said that bringing R.E.P.O. to consoles is the current plan, but console development is not expected to become a major focus until the game is closer to its 1.0 release. There is no confirmed PS5 release date, no PlayStation Store version to play, and no official PS5 launch window. A planned console version is not the same thing as an announced release date.

Is R.E.P.O. on Xbox? R.E.P.O. is not currently released on Xbox either. The developer's public console statement did not announce separate Xbox or PlayStation dates. It only confirmed that a console release is part of the plan for the future. Until semiwork announces specific platforms and dates, Xbox players should treat any exact release date circulating online as speculation.

Is R.E.P.O. on Console? Not yet. The current public version is the Windows PC version sold through Steam. The official Steam system requirements list Windows 10 as the minimum operating system and Windows 11 as the recommended operating system. semiwork has publicly said that a console release is planned, but development on it is expected later in the road toward R.E.P.O. 1.0.

Is R.E.P.O. Crossplay? There is currently no PC-to-PS5 or PC-to-Xbox crossplay because R.E.P.O. has not yet released on those consoles. The current game supports online multiplayer on its existing PC release. semiwork's 2026 console statement confirms plans to investigate a console release later in development, but it does not confirm a future crossplay system. R.E.P.O. does not currently have PC-console crossplay, and future crossplay has not been officially confirmed.

Is R.E.P.O. Cross Platform? Not in the usual PC/PlayStation/Xbox sense right now. R.E.P.O. currently has one public PC release rather than separate PC, PlayStation, and Xbox versions that can play together. If a console version is released later, cross-platform multiplayer will depend on what semiwork chooses to support at that time.

When Is R.E.P.O. Coming to PS5 or Xbox? There is no confirmed date. In its March 2026 Q&A, semiwork said a console release is the current plan but that the team would not fully dig into console development until it was on the homestretch toward the 1.0 update. That gives players a development direction, not a launch window. Do not treat third-party countdowns, store placeholders, or predicted dates as official unless semiwork announces them.

Can You Play R.E.P.O. on PC Now? Yes. R.E.P.O. is available through Steam for Windows PC. The game remains in Early Access, so its supported platforms and features may expand as development continues.

Does R.E.P.O. Support Multiplayer? Yes. The Steam store describes R.E.P.O. as an online co-op horror game where you can play with up to five friends. That means a lobby can support up to six players total. For player-count details and team-role suggestions, see the RUNBACK multiplayer guide.
mistakes: Treating a planned console release as a dated announcement, treating third-party predictions as official, or assuming future crossplay is confirmed.
versionNote: Platform availability, console development, and future multiplayer support can change. This page reports the current public Windows PC release and semiwork's stated development direction without predicting a launch date.
